---
title: "Workspace, Attempts, Receipts, and Artifacts"
subtitle: "How is durable evidence appended and resolved safely?"
toc-depth: 2
---

**Status:** `CONVERGING` implementation design.

## Bind one leaf workspace to one Plan

A V1 leaf workspace is a relocatable directory with one sealed Plan plus
append-only request attempts. Each request carries its own semantic runtime:

```text
workspace.json
plan.json
requests/<request-sha256>/
  request.json
  attempts/000001/
    attempt.json
    logs/
    artifacts/result.zarr/
    result.json
    receipt.json
```

The workspace location is not part of computational request identity. It
selects the evidence store in which that request must be found; relocating the
whole verified workspace does not rename the request. All stored paths are
relative to the workspace. `receipt.json` is written last and only after Python
verifies the attempt outcome. It seals success, typed failure, or interruption;
only a verified success receipt can materialize a Result. A temporary staging
directory is never a successful Result.

V1 uses one writer lock per workspace; different workspaces may run in
parallel. This deliberately simple ceiling avoids two processes selecting the
same next attempt number or sealing competing successes. Per-request locking
is considered only if measured same-workspace throughput requires it.

## Iterate topology in one workspace {#iterate-topology-in-one-workspace}

`CircuitRun(..., versioned=False)` is the default Notebook behavior. Reopening
the same path with the same Plan identity reuses its evidence. A different Plan
is validated and sealed first, then an exclusive lock, sibling staging
directory, and atomic rename replace the old leaf workspace. No prompt,
recycle area, or implicit topology history is added. A prior Run or lazy Result
whose bound leaf `workspace_instance_id` or Plan no longer matches that path
raises
`WorkspacePlanReplacedError` instead of reading unrelated evidence.

Every replacement creates a new evidence-only leaf instance ID. This keeps an
old Run stale through an `A → B → A` topology sequence instead of accepting the
later A workspace merely because its Plan hash matches again.

With `versioned=True`, the selected path is a parent index:

```text
workspace.json
iteration01/
  workspace.json
  plan.json
  requests/...
iteration02/
  workspace.json
  plan.json
  requests/...
```

Each `iterationNN` is an ordinary leaf workspace. The parent maps exact Plan
hashes to monotonically assigned directories, using at least two decimal
digits. Reopening the same Plan reuses its existing iteration; only a new Plan
identity allocates the next ordinal. Specs and ParameterSets remain requests
inside that iteration.

Index entries are stored in ascending ordinal order. Ordinals and directories
are unique, every Plan hash appears once, and `next_iteration` is one greater
than the greatest existing ordinal (or `1` when empty). These cross-entry
invariants are semantic validation in addition to the JSON Schema shape. The
parent and all leaf workspace-instance IDs are also mutually distinct.

Opening an existing unversioned leaf with `versioned=True` is a supported,
atomic one-way conversion: the leaf becomes `iteration01` and the parent index
is written around it without changing its leaf instance or request identities;
the new parent receives its own instance ID. Opening a
versioned parent with `versioned=False` raises
`WorkspaceVersioningDowngradeForbidden` before mutation. The message explains
that versioning was an explicit preservation choice and directs the user to a
different workspace path for replacement mode.

A pre-upgrade Run follows its preserved leaf instance into `iteration01` after
the conversion. It does not become stale merely because the user enabled
preservation; subsequent replacements of that leaf remain detectable by its
instance ID.

## Reuse success and append failure history

The request directory is derived from canonical request identity. If one
attempt contains a complete verified success, the terminal operation returns
it. Otherwise a new call appends the next immutable attempt. Failed and
interrupted attempts remain visible to `inventory()` and cannot be overwritten.

A verified `HBBatchResult` is successful request evidence even when every case
contains a numerical `HBCaseFailure`; repeating it reuses the batch. Only a
request-level failure or interruption is retryable.

`resolve()` acquires no execution slot. It recomputes the request identity,
finds the verified success, and validates Plan, semantic runtime, receipt, manifest, and
artifact hashes. Missing or corrupt evidence is an error; it never falls back
to another attempt or request.

## Store arrays without pickling

Scalar metadata, schemas, failures, and receipts use canonical JSON. Large real
arrays use Zarr V2 chunks; complex arrays use paired Float64 real/imag arrays
with one typed manifest. V1 starts with uncompressed chunks so another language
can implement the format without a codec dependency. The OGC-endorsed
[Zarr V2 standard](https://www.ogc.org/standards/zarr-storage-specification/)
defines JSON metadata and optionally compressed binary chunks for
multidimensional arrays.

Chunk shape, array order, dtype, axes, units, coordinate IDs, and real/imag
pairing are manifest authority. A Python Result may load chunks lazily, but
must reconstruct the declared NumPy/Pint surface before returning it.

The exact envelopes and Result/artifact references are defined by the
[machine-readable identity schemas](canonical-identities-and-schemas.qmd).
